To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) rumor centrality is a novel network centrality measure, which is an ML estimator in trees and performs well in general networks; (ii) on trees that grow faster than a straight line, the estimator will always have non-trivial detection probabilities as the network grows, whereas on trees growing like a straight line, detection probability goes to 0 as network size grows; (iii) the rumor center is the same as the distance center on trees but may differ on general graphs, and
(a) rumor centrality is a good measure of network centrality, (b) it is an ML estimator of virus source, and (c) it is more accurate in finding the virus source than the popular distance centrality.
rumor centrality is a ML estimator for the virus center in trees, and rumor centrality out-performs distance centrality as a virus source detector in general networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
a new class of network centrality notions which are designed to solve problems in network epidemiology.
the problem of finding a virus source in a network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rumor centrality is a good estimator for virus source detection in networks.
rumor centrality provides a very good estimator for the source of computer viruses in a variety of network topologies.
rumor centrality is a good estimator for the source of a virus on a variety of network topologies, including real networks, and that it outperforms distance-centrality in many cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rumor centrality is an efficient and accurate estimator for the virus sources in networks, and is robust to network structure.
rumor centrality is the right notion of centrality to use for detecting virus sources in networks.
rumor centrality is a good measure of the likelihood that a node is the source of the virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an important difference between the notions of rumor centrality and distance centrality, and that the former is more suitable for the problem of finding virus sources in computer networks.

there is a fundamental distinction between tree-like and non-tree-like network topologies, in terms of how easy it is to detect the source of a virus in a network, and that rumor centrality provides a natural way to quantify the ease of detecting the source of a network virus in both types of networks.
rumor centrality provides a powerful tool for finding the source of virus infections on real-world networks.
